issue.title: check-full flake-baseline gate exits 2: duplicate fixed-at entry for test_dev_extension_exposes_every_collected_name
issue.description:
`tools/selection_health --fail-on-new-flake` (the "flake baseline" step, the last gate
of `just check-full` at Justfile:907) exits 2 on master HEAD 60832648be before
judging any flake:

  flake baseline gate: tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt:408: duplicate fixed-at
  entry for tests/test_check_sase_core_rs_bindings_tool.py::test_dev_extension_exposes_every_collected_name

ROOT CAUSE: the baseline holds two `# fixed-at:` directives for the same node:
- line 380: `# fixed-at: 2026-09-08T22:11:29Z ...` (added by a5e642c929, 2026-09-08)
- line 408: `# fixed-at: 2026-09-22T13:25:12Z ...` (added by e8d238688f, 2026-09-22)
The baseline parser in tools/selection_health (~L112-115) raises ValueError on a
duplicate fixed-at node, so every `just check-full` since 2026-09-22 ends red on its
flake-baseline step no matter what the test records say.

Fix: keep one directive per node. Keep the later 2026-09-22 instant (it retires the
evidence of both fixes) with a preceding comment naming both commits, and drop the
other. Then rerun `.venv/bin/python tools/selection_health --fail-on-new-flake` and
confirm it reaches a real verdict.

Related cleanup in the same file (optional; it does not affect the exit code):
several baseline entries point at flake beads closed as fixed in the 2026-10-26
backlog triage and can become fixed-at retirements or be removed: sase-sf, sase-xb,
sase-12h, and sase-x6 (lines ~307-309 still list the pre-split node ids). The sase-12a
entry also has a stale path.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic parse error: tools/selection_health raises ValueError('duplicate fixed-at entry') when it loads the baseline, before reading any test records. Reproduced at 60832648be with exit 2.

issue.creation_reason: The last gate of just check-full has failed on every run since 2026-09-22 because of a baseline parse error, not a real flake verdict; no bead tracks it. Found during the 2026-10-26 task-bead backlog triage.
